parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Test how water temperature affects sugar dissolving time. Name what you change, what you measure and one thing you keep the same.
ms: Change water temperature.
Measure time taken for sugar to dissolve.
Keep sugar mass, water volume, stirring or sugar grain size the same.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: An empty balance reads 3 g. What type of error is this? How does it affect readings, and how would you fix it?
ms: It is a systematic or zero error.
Readings are all 3 g too high.
Set the balance to zero or calibrate it before measuring.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A microscope has a ×12 eyepiece and ×10 objective. Find total magnification. Give one rule for drawing a clear cell diagram.
ms: Multiply 12 × 10.
Total magnification = ×120.
Use clear single lines, straight label lines or suitable proportions.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Name three structures in a typical leaf cell that are not found in a typical animal cell.
ms: A cell wall.
Chloroplasts.
A large permanent vacuole.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Why do muscles work as an opposing pair to bend and straighten a joint?
ms: Muscles pull rather than actively push.
One muscle contracts to move the joint one way.
The other contracts to move it back.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Use particles to explain why a gas fills its container but a solid keeps its shape.
ms: Gas particles move freely with large gaps.
They spread throughout the available space.
Solid particles vibrate around fixed positions.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: How would you get salt crystals from a dry mixture of salt and sand?
ms: Add water to dissolve the salt.
Filter out the sand.
Evaporate some water and leave the solution to form crystals.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A lamp takes in 240 J and gives 36 J as useful light. Find its efficiency and the unwanted energy transfer.
ms: Efficiency = 36 ÷ 240 = 0.15.
Efficiency = 15%.
Unwanted energy = 240 − 36 = 204 J.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A 1.5 kW heater runs for 2 hours. Electricity costs 24 p per kWh. Find the energy used and the cost.
ms: Energy = 1.5 × 2 = 3 kWh.
Cost = 3 × 24.
Cost = 72 p.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: How are inherited and environmental differences different? Give one example of each.
ms: Inherited differences come from genes passed on by parents.
Environmental differences come from surroundings or experiences.
Examples include inherited ABO blood group and an environmental scar; accept other correct examples.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: What are fertilisation and implantation in humans? Say where each usually happens.
ms: Sperm and egg nuclei join at fertilisation.
Fertilisation usually happens in an oviduct, also called a fallopian tube.
The embryo later attaches to the uterus lining at implantation.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: Describe two features of an insect-pollinated flower. Explain how a feature helps pollination.
ms: A feature such as bright petals or scent.
It attracts insects that can carry pollen.
Nectar attracts insects, or sticky pollen attaches to them; link a second feature to its job.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: How is pollination different from fertilisation in a flowering plant? Include the step that links them.
ms: Pollination moves pollen from anther to stigma.
A pollen tube grows towards an ovule.
At fertilisation, male and egg nuclei join.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Name three conditions most seeds need to germinate. Explain why one is needed.
ms: Water.
Oxygen.
A suitable temperature, plus an explanation such as oxygen being needed for aerobic respiration.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: A pupil says every strong acid must be concentrated. Why are these words different?
ms: Strength describes how much the acid splits into charged particles in water.
Concentration describes how much acid is in a given volume of solution.
A strong acid can be dilute if mixed with plenty of water.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. Name the products and describe a test for the gas.
ms: Zinc chloride.
Hydrogen.
A small sample makes a squeaky pop with a lighted splint in a teacher-supervised test.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Magnesium is more reactive than copper. What happens when magnesium is put into copper sulfate solution? Explain why.
ms: Magnesium displaces copper.
Magnesium sulfate and copper form.
Magnesium replaces copper because it is more reactive.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Two parallel branches carry 0.35 A and 0.45 A. Find the supply current and explain your method.
ms: Supply current = 0.80 A.
Total current into a junction equals total current out.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A resistor has 9 V across it and a current of 0.3 A. Find its resistance. How should the voltmeter be connected?
ms: Resistance = voltage ÷ current.
Connect the voltmeter in parallel across the resistor.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: A ball bounces lower each time. Why is the total energy of the ball and its surroundings still conserved?
ms: Less energy remains in the ball for movement and height.
Energy transfers to heating and sound in the surroundings.
The energy is not destroyed, so the total stays the same.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: In grass → grasshopper → bird, grasshopper numbers fall. What might happen to the grass and birds? Give one reason your prediction may not be exact.
ms: Grass may increase because less is eaten.
Birds may decline because they have less food.
Other food sources or other changes in the food web could affect the result.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: How could you use quadrats to estimate how many plants grow in a field?
ms: Place equal-sized quadrats at random points and count consistently.
Calculate a mean number per square metre from several samples.
Multiply by field area and state that the answer is an estimate.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A trolley travels 3.6 m in 6 seconds. Find its average speed. Give one way to reduce timing error.
ms: Speed = 3.6 ÷ 6.
Speed = 0.6 m/s.
Use electronic timing or a longer timed distance to reduce the effect of reaction time.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Describe the forces on a skydiver falling at terminal velocity. Why is the speed steady?
ms: Weight acts downwards.
Drag acts upwards with the same size as weight.
The forces balance, so speed does not change.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: What is an element, a compound and a mixture? Give an example of each.
ms: An element contains one type of atom, such as iron.
A compound has different elements chemically joined, such as water.
A mixture contains substances not chemically joined to each other, such as air.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: How does reactivity change down Groups 1 and 7? Chlorine is more reactive than bromine. Can it displace bromine from a bromide solution?
ms: Group 1 generally gets more reactive down the group.
Group 7 generally gets less reactive down the group.
Yes. Chlorine displaces the less reactive bromine.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Give three features that help alveoli exchange gases quickly.
ms: A large surface area.
Thin walls give a short distance for gases to travel.
A good blood supply and fresh air maintain concentration differences.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: How do enzymes and villi help digested nutrients reach the blood?
ms: Enzymes break large food molecules into small soluble ones.
Villi give a large surface area for absorption.
Small molecules pass through the thin gut wall into the blood.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: What does a positive iodine test look like? What can and cannot be concluded from a negative result?
ms: A blue-black colour shows starch was detected.
A negative result means starch was not detected in that test.
Other carbohydrates, such as sugars, may still be present.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Why should young people not describe nicotine vaping as harmless? Give three points.
ms: Nicotine can cause dependence, making it difficult to stop.
It can affect health and the developing body.
Less harmful than smoking does not mean harmless or suitable for children and non-smokers.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: A wave has frequency 8 Hz and wavelength 0.5 m. Find its speed. What does frequency mean?
ms: Speed = frequency × wavelength.
Speed = 8 × 0.5 = 4 m/s.
Frequency is the number of complete vibrations each second.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: How is a higher-pitched sound different from a louder sound?
ms: A higher pitch means a higher frequency.
A louder sound usually has a larger amplitude.
Pitch and loudness can change separately.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A ray hits a plane mirror at 28° to the normal. Find the reflection angle and the angle to the mirror surface.
ms: The reflection angle is 28° to the normal.
The normal is at 90° to the mirror.
The angle to the mirror surface is 90 − 28 = 62°.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A reaction in an open flask gives off gas and the measured mass falls. Why has mass not been destroyed?
ms: Gas leaves the flask.
The gas still exists outside the flask.
Counting all reactants and products, including the gas, gives the same total mass.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Explain why an exothermic reaction warms its surroundings. Include breaking and making bonds.
ms: Breaking old bonds takes in energy.
Making new bonds releases energy.
More energy is released than taken in, so the extra energy warms the surroundings.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: A catalyst gives more gas after 30 seconds but the same final gas volume. Explain why.
ms: A catalyst speeds up the reaction.
The same starting amounts can make the same total gas.
The reaction finishes sooner rather than making extra product.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Write the word equation for aerobic respiration. How is respiration different from breathing?
ms: Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.
Respiration is a chemical process in cells that releases energy.
Breathing moves air into and out of the lungs.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Name the two products of yeast fermentation. Explain how one helps bread making.
ms: Ethanol.
Carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide bubbles make the dough rise.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Why might brighter light stop increasing oxygen production by pondweed?
ms: At first, too little light slowed photosynthesis.
Another factor, such as carbon dioxide, may now be in short supply.
Extra light alone cannot remove that other limit.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Dye spreads faster in warm water. Give one control and explain why the result may not be due to diffusion alone.
ms: Keep dye amount, water volume or container size the same and do not stir.
Convection currents can carry the coloured water.
The colour spreading therefore does not measure diffusion alone.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Why does a compass turn near a bar magnet? Which way do field arrows point outside the magnet?
ms: A compass needle is a small magnet.
It turns to line up with the magnetic field.
Field arrows outside a magnet point from north to south.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: How does an electromagnet operate a relay switch? Give one benefit of this type of magnet.
ms: Current in a coil makes a magnetic field.
The magnet pulls a metal part to operate a switch.
Switching the current lets you turn the magnet on and off.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A 30 N force moves a load 2.5 m in its direction. Find the work done. What does the unit mean?
ms: Work done = force × distance.
A joule is a unit of energy transferred.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A 15 N force acts 0.4 m from a pivot. What force on the opposite side, 0.6 m away, balances it?
ms: First moment = 15 × 0.4 = 6 N m.
The other force × 0.6 must equal 6 N m.
Other force = 6 ÷ 0.6 = 10 N.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: How does a vacuum flask reduce conduction, convection and radiation?
ms: The vacuum greatly reduces conduction across the gap because it has almost no particles.
The vacuum prevents convection across the gap.
Shiny surfaces reduce infrared radiation transfer.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: How can burning fossil fuels change the carbon cycle and warm Earth?
ms: Burning moves carbon from fuel into the air as carbon dioxide.
Extra carbon dioxide absorbs more outgoing infrared radiation and sends some back towards the surface.
This changes the energy balance and causes warming.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Why can carbon extract some metals from their oxides, while aluminium is usually extracted using electricity?
ms: The metal reactivity affects the extraction method.
Carbon can remove oxygen from oxides of less reactive metals.
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so electricity is used instead.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Give two environmental benefits and one drawback of recycling metals.
ms: It saves limited metal ores.
It often uses less energy and reduces mining damage.
Collection, sorting and processing still use resources.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Describe natural selection in three linked steps.
ms: Individuals have inherited differences.
Those with helpful features are more likely to survive and reproduce.
They pass on genes, so helpful features can become more common over generations.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Why might a breeding programme alone not save an endangered species in the wild?
ms: Enough animals must breed successfully with enough inherited variation.
They also need a safe, suitable habitat.
If threats remain, released animals may not survive and reproduce.

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: How are DNA, chromosomes, genes and alleles related?
ms: Chromosomes contain long DNA molecules.
Genes are sections of DNA.
Alleles are different versions of a gene.

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: In a simple dominant model, cross Aa with Aa. Give the genotype ratio and the chance of the recessive feature.
ms: Possible combinations are AA, Aa, Aa and aa.
The genotype ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa.
The recessive feature has a 1 in 4 chance.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: An ultrasound echo returns after 0.00008 seconds. Sound speed is 1500 m/s. How deep is the reflecting surface?
ms: Total distance = 1500 × 0.00008 = 0.12 m.
Divide by two for the outward and return journeys.
Depth = 0.06 m.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Compare sound and electromagnetic waves. Which need a material to travel through, and which can be ionising?
ms: Sound needs a material, but electromagnetic waves can cross empty space.
Sound is not ionising.
Some high-energy electromagnetic waves, such as X-rays, can ionise atoms and damage cells.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: How do igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks form?
ms: Igneous rock forms when molten rock cools and becomes solid.
Sedimentary rock often forms when layers of sediment are pressed and cemented together.
Metamorphic rock forms when heat and pressure change rock without melting it.

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Why do normal Moon phases happen? Why are they different from an eclipse?
ms: The Moon reflects sunlight and roughly half is lit.
Its orbit changes how much of the lit half we can see.
The shadow of Earth causes a lunar eclipse, not normal phases.

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Explain the seasons on Earth using its tilted axis. Why does summer not depend mainly on Earth being closer to the Sun?
ms: The axis of Earth is tilted.
The hemisphere tilted towards the Sun has longer days.
It also receives more direct sunlight, while the other hemisphere has winter.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A 5 N force extends a spring by 0.025 m. Find the spring constant. State when this calculation is valid.
ms: Spring constant = force ÷ extension.
The spring must be within the straight-line force–extension range, below its limit of proportionality.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A 480 N force acts over 0.024 m². Find the pressure. What if the area doubles while force stays the same?
ms: Doubling area halves pressure at the same force.
The new pressure is 10,000 Pa.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: How can a hydraulic system give a larger output force without creating extra energy?
ms: A pressure change is passed through the enclosed liquid.
A larger output piston area gives a larger force.
The larger piston moves a shorter distance, so no extra energy is created.
